Drawing From a Separable Penalty

Source: R/penalty_draw.R
penalty_draw.DistribPenalty.Rd

Draws from the parent family, one draw per coordinate for a univariate parent and one per block for a multivariate parent, carried back through the map.

Arguments

penalty

A DistribPenalty() object.

theta

Its hyperparameters, which are the parent's parameters.

...

Ignored.

Value

A numeric vector of length penalty@n_coef, NA where a diagonal map has a zero entry and NA throughout under a map that is not diagonal.

Details

The penalty is the parent's negative log-density applied to each coordinate (or block) of \(D\beta\), so a draw is distributions7::distrib_rng() at the hyperparameters, which are the parent's own parameters. Under a multivariate parent the draw has one row per block and is flattened in the order in which dp_arg() reads it.

A diagonal map is inverted by dividing, since the prior is on \(d_j\beta_j\). A coordinate whose \(d_j\) is zero is not determined by the prior and is NA, and the other coordinates are drawn as usual. A square map whose off-diagonal entries are all zero is stored as a diagonal map by distrib_penalty(), whatever its class, and is treated in the same way. Under any other map every coordinate is NA.

See also

penalty_draw(), distrib_penalty()
